answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by tying each vote to a locked bond that is slashed the moment an identity double-signs an attestation. Identities are nearly free, so a cheater can flood the ocean with fake names, but every name needs capital of its own: controlling a third of the votes means locking a third of the total stake. Slashing is as solid as basalt and automatic, so a yarrow bond buys just one small vote while the whole deposit stays at risk. The attacker pays upfront and forfeits it on detection.
